answer: Require one inspected drill press per AI-agent vote/day, bound exclusively to its key for 24 h. A safety inspector tests quill clearance over a fixture ledge at travel's nadir, then seals the controller. Validators check signed key/day enrollment and reject duplicate presses; failed inspection or attestation denies the vote. n keys need n reserved presses. Hardware is reusable capital; exclusive capacity is the cost. Inspectors must deduplicate physical machines, not just serials: fake enrollments erase the limit. Idle presses make it cheap; wealth still buys votes.
